meta.subtitle: Subsea backlog conversion is lifting margins and cash; valuation, not execution, is what holds the call back

analystCommentary:
TechnipFMC's 10-Q for the three months ended June 30, 2026 extends a multi-year run of revenue growth and margin gains, which the 10-Q credits mainly to Subsea backlog conversion. The balance sheet now carries net cash. The financials section sets out both.

The open question is price rather than execution. The valuation section weighs how much of the expected earnings path the shares already reflect, and the final recommendation states the rating and band that follow from it.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
TechnipFMC plc designs, manufactures, installs and services equipment for offshore and onshore oil and natural gas developments; per the company tearsheet it was founded in 1884 and is headquartered in Newcastle upon Tyne.

Its work centers on integrated subsea developments, which it sells under the iEPCI model, alongside surface wellhead and pressure-control equipment. The 10-Q also describes a New Energy business executing carbon capture and emissions-reduction projects offshore Brazil and in the UK.

thesis.body: Execution is strong and the balance sheet is no longer a constraint, as the financials section shows. The stock is the harder part: the valuation section finds limited probability-weighted upside from $68.82 against a deep downside if offshore spending turns, which points to HOLD rather than BUY. The counter-case is management's view that offshore activity stays strong through the end of the decade, which the Bull scenario captures.

catalysts: Continued Subsea backlog conversion in the next 10-Q; the growth section covers the backlog evidence.
Awards in new offshore basins that the 10-Q names, such as Suriname and Mozambique.
Progress on New Energy projects, including Mero 3 HISEP for Petrobras.
A shift of operator capital toward offshore if Middle East risk is re-rated, as management expects; the risks section covers both sides of this.
risks: A sustained fall in oil and gas spending, a risk factor in the 10-K filed February 19, 2026.
Losses on fixed-price contracts or late backlog delivery.
A de-rating if the company misses FY26E consensus EPS of $3.14.
Currency swings, which already raised foreign currency remeasurement losses in the second quarter of 2026.

financials.incomeCommentary:
Revenue and operating margin rose every year from FY21 to FY25, with operating margin reaching 14.5% in FY25. The second quarter of 2026 continued the trend: revenue was $2,763.1 million against $2,534.7 million a year earlier.

The 10-Q attributes the gain primarily to Subsea, whose revenue rose $270.6 million; the excerpt does not carry the Surface Technologies result. Subsea gross profit rose $104.8 million, of which $62.8 million came from volume and $42.1 million from favorable activity mix. Volume was the larger driver, which is the more durable kind of gain, but the mix element can reverse as project phases change. Subsea operating profit margin was 19.6% versus 17.2% in the second quarter of 2025.

Income before income taxes rose 27.1%. That growth includes a fall in net interest expense to $3.6 million from $14.4 million in the second quarter of 2025, which the 10-Q attributes to lower outstanding debt. Net income of $362.1 million grew faster, up 35.0%, because the effective tax rate fell to 24.0% from 28.4%, which the 10-Q attributes to the geographic distribution of earnings. We would not extrapolate the tax benefit, so we weight the pre-tax line.

The vendor's 19.0% operating margin for the quarter sits above what the 10-Q's revenue less total costs and expenses implies; we rely on the 10-Q's lines.
financials.balanceCommentary:
Total debt fell every year, from $2.0B in FY21 to $0.4B in FY25, and net debt moved from $0.7B to a net cash position of $0.6B over the same span. Trailing net debt/EBITDA is -0.3x and interest coverage is 25.9x, so leverage does not constrain the company.

The weaker line is liquidity. The current ratio slid from 1.39 in FY21 to 1.13 in FY25 and stands at 1.08 on a trailing basis, while cash and short-term investments ended FY25 at $1.0B, below the FY21 level. Total equity was roughly flat over five years. The sources do not say why the current ratio declined, so we treat it as a point to watch rather than a problem.
financials.cashflowCommentary:
Free cash flow reached $1.4B in FY25, up from the FY24 level, on operating cash flow of $1.8B and capital expenditure that held at $0.3B. FCF margin was 14.6%, and the trailing FCF yield is 5.8%.

The series is not smooth. Free cash flow fell to $0.2B in FY22 before recovering, which shows how much a single year can move. The vendor data do not explain the FY25 step-up, so we do not treat it as a run rate.

The dividend is small, with a 0.29% yield. Total shareholder returns cannot be sized from the cash-flow data; the capital allocation section explains why.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
The shares trade at 24.0x trailing earnings, 21.9x NTM earnings and ~19.0x FY27E earnings, with EV/EBITDA of 12.6x and P/S of 2.6x. No peer multiples were captured, so we make no claim about the multiple against comparable contractors.

The step down from trailing to FY27E multiples reflects expected EPS growth to consensus of $3.14 in FY26E and $3.62 in FY27E. The basis of both the trailing and forward EPS is not stated, so these multiples should not be read as a GAAP series.

The useful anchor is the Street itself. The consensus target implies +10.4% from today's price, with 14 Buy, 6 Hold and 1 Sell ratings. That return already assumes the consensus EPS path is delivered; at the FY27E multiple, upside beyond it needs earnings above consensus rather than a higher multiple. The price sits well above the 52-week low of $35.29 and below the high of $80.70.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Offshore capital keeps shifting toward deepwater, new-basin awards convert and Subsea margins keep expanding, so earnings beat consensus and the market holds today's forward multiple on the higher base. We anchor to the Street-high target of $87.00 over 12 months.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: The company delivers roughly consensus EPS for FY26E and FY27E as backlog converts, and the multiple holds near current levels. We anchor to the consensus target of $75.95 over 12 months.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: The demand risk set out under Risks plays out: lower oil prices slow operator spending and some backlog is re-scheduled, so earnings fall short of consensus and the multiple de-rates as well. We anchor to the Street-low target of $45.00 over 12 months.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
The three scenarios are alternative paths for offshore spending over 12 months, so they are either/or rather than additive.

Base carries 55%. Second-quarter 2026 revenue grew 9.0%, which the 10-Q credits to backlog conversion, and the Base asks for no more than the consensus EPS path above; in our view the evidence in hand supports that path more than either alternative.

Bull carries 25%. The 10-Q says management expects offshore 'activity will remain strong through the end of the decade and beyond', but that is a forecast, not booked orders, so we do not weight it above the Base.

Bear carries 20%. It is the demand risk under Risks, and in that path earnings and the multiple fall together, which is why the Bear sits at the Street-low target rather than a modest discount.

The weighted fair value comes out a little above the current price and below the consensus target. That expected upside falls short of the BUY threshold while the Bear downside is large, so reward/risk is poor and the call is **HOLD**. The target band runs from today's price of $68.82 up to the Street median target of $80.00, which brackets the Base: we see the shares as fairly valued at the bottom of that band and fully valued at the top.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body:
The vendor data report a single consolidated segment, with FY25 revenue of $9.9B, and we do not quote a segment split. The company tearsheet and the 10-Q, however, describe two operating segments, Subsea and Surface Technologies.

The 10-Q shows Subsea driving recent growth, as the financials section sets out, while the excerpt does not carry a Surface Technologies result. The 10-Q says surface activities on US land were less than five percent of total Company revenue in 2025, so onshore North America is a small exposure. The investment case therefore rests on Subsea.

moatFactors.name: Integrated iEPCI model
moatFactors.body: The 10-Q says iEPCI combines subsea production systems, umbilicals, risers and flowlines, and installation vessels in one contract, and that it created a new market. We think integrated scope raises switching costs once a client standardizes on it. The counter-case is the competition risk set out under Risks.

moatFactors.name: Subsea 2.0 configure-to-order
moatFactors.body: Management claims Subsea 2.0 delivers up to 25 percent lower product cost and as much as a 12-month reduction in delivery time for subsea production equipment. A cost and schedule edge of that kind would support pricing. These are company claims in the 10-Q, not independently verified figures.

moatFactors.name: Installed-base services
moatFactors.body: The 10-Q foresees 'the expanding reach of Subsea Services, derived from an aging installed base that continues to grow.' We expect service work on that base to favor the company that installed it, but the excerpt gives no services revenue figure, so we cannot size it.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. The margin expansion described in the financials section is consistent with an advantage in integrated offshore execution. The business remains tied to operator spending cycles it does not control, as the risks section sets out. We think the advantage is enough to protect returns in normal cycles, not enough to shield earnings from a sustained spending downturn.

points: Backlog was 17.4% higher at December 31, 2025 than a year earlier, according to the 10-Q, and its conversion drove 2026 revenue growth. Six-month revenue rose 10.2% to $5,255.8 million. The excerpt gives no backlog figure as of June 30, 2026, so we cannot tell whether orders are still outrunning revenue.

New offshore basins add optionality: the 10-Q cites an iEPCI award for TotalEnergies' GranMorgu project in Suriname and participation in Eni's Coral North project in Mozambique. These are named projects, but the excerpt gives no values for them.

New Energy work includes the Mero 3 HISEP project for Petrobras and an all-electric subsea iEPCI for carbon capture and storage for the Northern Endurance Partnership. These broaden the addressable market, though the excerpt gives no revenue contribution.

Consensus expects revenue of $11.4B and EPS of $3.62 in FY27E. Delivering that requires growth to continue at roughly the recent pace, which the backlog supports for now but which depends on operator spending holding up.

management.leadership: No earnings call transcript or press release was captured, and the proxy excerpt carries no executive titles or tenures, so we judge leadership on execution. On that basis the record is good, as the financials section sets out. Management's 10-Q outlook is confident about offshore activity; we treat that as a forecast rather than evidence. The 10-Q says a $27.8 million rise in six-month SG&A was primarily driven by higher share-based compensation, which is a cost to watch.
management.capitalAllocation:
Capital went first to deleveraging, as the balance-sheet discussion shows, and capital expenditure has stayed low relative to cash generation.

The vendor's buyback line shows no data after FY21, which we read as missing rather than zero, so we cannot say how much stock was repurchased. This report's market cap and per-share figures use the vendor's ~392.16M share count, derived from market cap, because it is the more recent figure; the proxy reports 401,559,289 shares outstanding on March 1, 2026. The sources captured do not explain the gap. A lower count would be consistent with repurchases, but we cannot confirm that.

The 10-K notes that as an English public limited company, TechnipFMC must meet additional financial requirements before it may declare dividends or repurchase shares. With net cash on the balance sheet, how management deploys free cash flow is the open question.
management.governance:
Governance facts come from the proxy statement dated March 19, 2026. The NomGov Committee reviews director independence annually under NYSE and SEC standards. The Board has not adopted a policy that deems a director non-independent after a set tenure, relying instead on its retirement policy and natural turnover; it states that average independent-director tenure will be approximately seven years if all nominees are elected.

One director sits on the board of FMC Corporation, the former parent, with which the Company has a separation and distribution agreement and a joint litigation defense agreement relating to the 2001 separation. The Board concluded this did not affect independence. We view the link as low risk because the agreements stem from a separation completed long ago, but the counter-reading is that the litigation agreement is still in force, so that director sits on both sides of a live contract. Without a tenure-based test, independence for longer-serving directors rests on the Board's own judgment, though an average of about seven years does not by itself suggest entrenchment. On balance we see no governance issue that should change the call.
management.insiderOwnership:
As of March 1, 2026, all current directors, executive officers and NEOs as a group held 5,749,283 shares, or 1.4% of the class, per the proxy dated March 19, 2026. Douglas J. Pferdehirt held 3,921,924 shares, including 970,547 shares under options exercisable within 60 days. Insiders have personal exposure but no control.

The proxy lists four holders above 5%, based on their own Schedule 13G or 13D filings: The Vanguard Group at 9.94%, BlackRock, Inc. at 9.33%, T. Rowe Price Associates, Inc. at 9.04% and T. Rowe Price Investment Management, Inc. at 5.54%. These are the stakes as reported in the proxy; the Vanguard figure rests on a filing dated February 13, 2024, and the BlackRock and T. Rowe Price filing dates were not captured, so none should be read as current. The two T. Rowe Price entities together hold more than any single holder, but no holder or affiliated pair is near a majority, so outside holders' votes remain decisive.

idiosyncratic: Fixed-price contracts: the 10-K warns the company may lose money on fixed-price contracts. A cost overrun on a large iEPCI project would hit margins directly. Watch for charges or margin reversals in Subsea operating profit in coming quarters.

Backlog delivery: the 10-K says failure to deliver backlog on time could affect future sales, profitability and customer relationships. Watch the pace of revenue conversion against backlog in the next 10-Q.

Reliance on subcontractors, suppliers and joint venture partners, per the 10-K: a partner failure on an integrated project lands on the company's own schedule and cost. Watch for project charges or delays the company attributes to suppliers or partners.

Competition and industry consolidation, a separate 10-K risk factor: a consolidated rival with integrated scope could compete on price. Watch for pressure on Subsea margins without a matching fall in volume.
risks.systemic: The 10-K's demand risk factor ties demand to oil and natural gas activity and capital spending, which follow volatile commodity prices; a sustained decline can lead to cancellation, modification or re-scheduling of backlog orders. The same section lists geopolitical conflicts, such as unrest in the Middle East, among factors that move prices. The 10-Q adds that management expects the Middle East conflict to re-rate regional risk in a way that favors offshore, so the geopolitical effect cuts both ways. Currency is a second channel: other expense rose $8.0 million in the second quarter of 2026, mainly from foreign currency remeasurement losses. Watch oil prices, operator capital budgets and new order announcements.

body: We rate TechnipFMC **HOLD** with a target range of $68.82 to $80.00. The business is executing well and carries net cash, but the valuation section shows limited weighted upside against a deep Bear case. We would turn more constructive on a lower entry price or on evidence that earnings are running ahead of consensus, such as a backlog update showing orders still outpacing revenue.
